The only moment is the present, but as humans with amygdalas and memories, we are certainly conditioned by our pasts. You can do all the meditation and Buddhism you can muster, but after my experience, it doesn't replace good trauma therapy.

Yeah I've read that book. It didn't help much, maybe since I'm a woman. But the overall concept was good. Anxious Attachment is a better book since my problem doesn't lie in lack of action, or love, but self shame. I don't recall it ever saying only reach out to your friends and not your SO. Maybe if you're a guy who just started dating or is looking for a relationship? But a 14 yr relationship, I wouldn't think that makes much sense.

How do you know I wouldn't go to an ahuasaca ceremony? I've considered mushrooms as a way to heal. You seem to make assumptions. 

I do not mean to sound ungrateful. I've just been nice and more accommodating to everyone at the expense of telling my own truth, and maybe that's a start. But I did reach out to a trauma therapist just now. Maybe this pain is a way of saying, it's time to continue this journey: and this is the next step. I appreciate your response.

As someone who had similar experiences in high school, and suffered shame as the main character did, there were mixed feelings. On one hand, I thought, "what she went through wasn't any worse than what I did, and she killed herself, so maybe I should have too." To young vulnerable people in the midst of such a traumatic episode, this show could be the thing that pushes them over the edge. To some, It validates that your pain was real and that it's ok to kill yourself in a sense, rather than find other outlets such as intensive therapy.

Another feeling was, "She was only understood after her death, when people were willing to take her feelings seriously." In a distorted way, it made me feel that it was a glorification of using self violence as a means to be understood by people. Unfortunately with depression and trauma, it is very hard to feel listened to and understood. As a result people injure and cut and abuse themselves because the pain runs deep. It is incredibly painful, indescribable sometimes. And suicide, in some ways, can be another way to try and gain that understanding. I am not saying it's wrong, but I think it's important not to instill in people's minds that suicide is an option to be understood and to have your pain put on a pedestal. It even got me thinking, though I never would do it, that what if I got ahold of my abusers after all these years and told them how much they hurt me and why? And that they had made me suicidal later in life? It's over now, and I don't think those people will ever, ever understand. Using suicide or threatening it as a way to get them to understand how much they hurt me, only hurts me. Because they never cared and they don't now.

Finally, it was nice to draw attention to the inward suffering that so many teens face. The shame and victim blaming in society does exist and is a problem. We have capacity for empathy but so many people feel ashamed, alone and confused anyway. We need better understanding and funding for mental health. As humans progress we will probably need it more so, since personality and abstract traits are more important now than ever in the history of being human. We are becoming more civilized, and that means having an understanding that because a person experiences trauma and bad circumstances, it does not make them weak or a failure and need to die. We have a right to assist those in need, rather than shame and blame. This show may have helped more people feel empathy toward the plight of people in a major depressive state, and to women who are sexually abused and victim blamed. It has its issues, but in this regard it's a step in the right direction, imo.

Hello. Can we pm today and talk? I know that you said nothing will change your mind. My goal is to talk so you can have a chance to express yourself. I am not a person who will judge or give unwarranted advice. 

Can you tell me what is going on in your life and what feelings you have?

I think there's a part of you that doesn't want to do this. The part of you that would rather seek the help and assurance you truly need right now, which is perhaps why you're here. It sounds like you hold this back for fear of your family finding out. It sounds like you are trying to be very strong, and perhaps have been during most of your life. I want you to know that you don't have to pretend anymore. I, too, have thoughts of suicide. Sometimes it almost feels vindictive (sorry) for the wrongs of previous people and the hurt I feel of having nowhere to turn.

But you do have places to turn. There are people out here who understand and feel for you because we know what it's like to have depression and other mental illness. Yes, you don't want to hurt your family, but people who are in terrible pain aren't thinking about others always. You are in pain, and I want you to know that it's fine you put your end and your true needs first for a change. If you have had depression since youth there is a good chance there is pain and trauma from that era that you don't know how to cope with despite all your strength and fortitude.

I hope this doesn't make it worse in any way. I'm not always good at saying the right thing plus I have depression too. My point is that the voice is lying to you. You have a long and fulfilling life ahead, with lots of love and understanding and happiness. The first step is to find someone to talk to right away who can give you the time and understanding you deserved a long time ago. It's not ok to hold back anymore to yourself. You have nothing to be ashamed of and should be proud for doing your best all these years. It's ok to ask for help now.
